gate2.variant_view: The market views the company as a secularly challenged media conglomerate weighed down by linear network erosion and high streaming content costs [D05]. We believe this discount fails to recognize the hidden value in its world-class parks and sports franchises, nor the significant margin expansion potential from rationalizing content spend and capital allocation [D01, D07]. By simplifying the portfolio and optimizing the balance sheet, the company can command a valuation commensurate with its unique asset base rather than its current bundled discount [D07].

final.memo:
The Walt Disney Company is a premier media conglomerate whose world-class assets—including its unmatched parks, streaming platform with 221 million subscribers, and critical sports rights—are obscured by a bundled valuation discount [D01, D03]. The market has penalized the company for secular network erosion and high content costs, yet we believe this view overlooks the hidden value in its unique ecosystem and the significant potential for margin expansion [D01, D05, D07].

Our sum-of-the-parts analysis values the business at $185.00 per share, compared to the current trading price of $124.26 [D04, D07]. By aligning its 16.6% segment operating margins with the 19.8% to 21.2% achieved by peers like Netflix and Comcast, the company can unlock substantial equity value [D06].

The market’s focus on short-term streaming headwinds misses the path to long-term profitability [D05]. We believe that by rationalizing content spend and streamlining the portfolio, the company can pivot from a conglomerate-burdened entity to a disciplined, best-in-class operator [D01, D07].

Our plan focuses on four key pillars: achieving a 20-21% margin target, evaluating the spin-off of non-core assets, optimizing capital allocation, and refreshing the board with relevant media and digital expertise [D06, D07]. We have initiated constructive private engagement following our HSR filing to press Bob Chapek and the Board on these priorities, with a two-quarter window for demonstrable progress [D01, D07].

Downside is protected by a solid $115.00 valuation floor derived from the recovery cycle in the parks division and the underlying strength of its sports franchises [D01, D04]. Should management remain entrenched or refuse to commit to these strategic improvements, we are prepared to escalate our involvement [D07].

We are initiating a 5% position in the common stock as of today, August 15, 2022 [D04, D07]. We are hedging our exposure to broader media sector beta using index puts to ensure our constructivist thesis remains decoupled from wider market volatility [D05, D08].
